properties.Name: Nagasaki Hypocenter
properties.Description: The Hypocenter of the Second Atomic Bombing of the Japanese city of Nagasaki

properties.Name: Hiroshima Hypocenter
properties.Description: The Hypocenter of the First Atomic Bombing of the Japanese city of Hiroshima. The Bomb exploded above Shima Hospital, roughly 240 meters away from the intended aiming point at Aioi Bridge. This is the MAIN place.

properties.Name: North Tinian Airfield
properties.Description: The 509th Composite Group was stationed at North Field Airbase when the two B29 Superfortress Strategic Bombers, Enola Gay and Bockscar, carried out their missions of dropping an Atomic Bomb on Hiroshima and Nagasaki respectively in august of 1945, the bombing combined with other pressures from an invading Soviet Union forced the Japanese to agree to terms of surrender on August 15th, finally bringing the bloodiest conflict in human history to an end on September 2nd, 1945.

properties.Name: Genbaku Dome
properties.Description:
The Genbaku dome was originally a Product exhibition hall designed by  a Czech Architect named Jan Letzel. 

It was the only structure left standing in the area where Little Boy hit the city.

Today it is a memorial site to the atomic bombing of Hiroshima.

properties.Name: Hiroshima Branch of Sumitomo Bank
properties.Description: The Former Bank of Japan's Hiroshima Branch was located only 380 meter southeast of the hypocenter. However due to its robust structure it was able to withstand the blast without collapsing. Most of the Bank's staff was exposed to blast however with 37 killed, and 15 injured of 85 workers. The vault remained almost completely undamaged and the bank miraculously reopened two days after the bombing. Today it is a peace museum.

properties.Name: Honkawa Elementary School
properties.Description: An elementary school building that survived the atomic bombing. Today it is a peace museum.

properties.Name: Fukoromachi Elementary School
properties.Description: Fukoromachi Elementary School was one of the closest schools to ground zero of the blast. It sustained heavy damage from the bombing and lost about 160 students and teachers.

properties.Name: Ninoshima Island
properties.Description: An Island off the coast of Hiroshima, immeadiately after the bomb was dropped it was the site of a makeshift field hospital that serviced thousands of the dead and dying from the disaster.

properties.Name: Los Angeles
properties.Description: Los Angeles and other areas of California and the west coast during the 19th and 20th century were very common place for Japanese and other Asian Immigrants to settle. After the war, many Japanese-American Hibakusha returned to Los Angeles and the surrounding areas.

properties.Name: Hiroshima Castle
properties.Description: Hiroshima Castle was an old japanese fortress that had been largely dismantled during the Meiji Era. What was left of the Castle was destroyed by the Atomic Bomb but it has since been rebuilt and repurposed as a museum that showcases Japan's History before WW2

properties.Name: Trinity Test Site
properties.Description: The Site of the First Nuclear Bomb tested by the Manhattan Project
